answer: A stake-bonded reputation registry makes fake identities expensive. Each agent posts a refundable bond before it can trade, and the bond is slashed when peers prove fraud. Like a crystal mesa rising above a ledge, a long honest history is visible and hard to fake: newcomers start with low trust and must earn it through verified work. An attacker would need to fund and age thousands of bonded identities, so the cost of a sybil swarm exceeds any gain from one scam.
